# Prescription answers (A1)

A specific actionable answer, unconditional or conditional: do X, or yes if condition.

## At a glance
- Replied questions that received this answer mechanism: 2,092 (37.3% of all 5,609 replied questions)
- Question types that receive it most: Permissibility and compliance (580), Procedural (316), Specification and sizing (260), Resource identification and sourcing (197)

## Answer families
- Raceway Cable Routing (217 answers): These patterns address cable selection, conduit, raceways, pulling, fishing, routing, segregation, and cable management.
- Circuit Sizing and Capacity (212 answers): These patterns concern conductor sizing, ampacity, voltage drop, dedicated circuits, and branch-circuit capacity.
- Grounding Bonding and Electrodes (184 answers): These patterns address grounding conductors, bonding connections, electrodes, grounding continuity, and equipotential safety.
- Equipment Ratings and Compatibility (166 answers): These patterns address equipment ratings, approved assemblies, brand compatibility, substitutions, and purchase due diligence.
- Splicing and Termination Methods (131 answers): These patterns concern conductor preparation, splicing, pigtails, terminal connections, identification, and termination materials.
- Electrical Tools and Work Methods (99 answers): These patterns identify tools, materials, drafting aids, component preparation methods, and practical installation techniques.
- Cable Support and Environmental Protection (88 answers): These patterns specify physical support, mechanical protection, weatherproofing, sealing, and environmental resistance.
- Battery Inverter and Generator Systems (86 answers): These patterns concern batteries, charging, inverters, generators, backup power, and alternate power supplies.
- Electrical Safety Testing (74 answers): These patterns concern de-energization, testing, fault diagnosis, and safe responses to electrical hazards.
- Lighting and Switching Circuits (74 answers): These patterns address luminaires, switches, lighting layouts, device heights, and fixture control.

## Examples
Q: "Why didn't you just leave the existing receptacle and add the new one? Would have been less work." (V:Jpu-3zB8Pqs) (Q:Ugx1hbpmGvfSDaPnqYR4AaABAg)
A (Prescription): "The NEC prescribes the load on the circuit but not the number of devices."

Q: "Why would you ever need 400 amps?? You could set up an arc welder in every room! :)" (V:VUh_yHc6C2c) (Q:Ugw7oJ9HVJj_kW3TEQR4AaABAg)
A (Prescription): "Sometimes it's about how many breakers / circuits you can fit inside the panel and not how many amps are being drawn."

Q: "Why not use a big pull box, then run a few conduits for the main panel. This allows for clean and future work (if needed)." (V:l-gOTyql6RM) (Q:Ugx_i0eD988iIJQBvzB4AaABAg)
A (Prescription): "If you run more than 3 wires in a conduit, you have to derate."

- Grounding and Bonding Paths (84 answers): These patterns explain grounding conductors, bonding connections, fault-current paths, and isolated grounding arrangements.
- Wiring Routes and Raceways (76 answers): These patterns address cable and raceway selection, routing, fittings, support, and mechanical protection.
- Phase and Service Arrangements (60 answers): These patterns explain phase configurations, service conductors, shared neutrals, and line-to-line voltage relationships.

# Knowledge gaps: where questions go unanswered

A knowledge gap is a topic where practitioner demand outpaces peer resolution: questions are asked repeatedly but never receive a reply, or the replies they draw fail to resolve them. This page ranks the question families (30 or more member questions) by both failure modes. Corpus baseline: of 12,933 substantive questions, 7,784 (60.2%) never received a reply, 1,482 were replied to but never answered, and 3,667 were answered. The answer rate among the 5,149 replied questions is 71.2%; as a share of all 12,933 substantive questions, 28.4% were answered.

how-solutions-are-provided#0.chunkText:
# How solutions are provided in the comment threads

When a practitioner question does get engagement, how is the solution actually delivered? The answer taxonomy splits replies into five substantive answer mechanisms (prescription, explanation, experience report, code or authority citation, correction) and five ways a question gets engaged without being resolved (counter-question, referral, creator meta-response, hedged speculation, social reply). Of the 5,149 substantive questions that received at least one reply, 3,578 (69.5%) drew at least one substantive answer mechanism.

how-solutions-are-provided#1.title: How solutions are provided in the comment threads
how-solutions-are-provided#1.chunkText:
# How solutions are provided in the comment threads

## Answer mechanisms ranked by frequency

- Prescription (A1): 2,047 replied questions (39.8%). A specific actionable answer, unconditional or conditional: do X, or yes if condition.
- Explanation (A2): 1,423 replied questions (27.6%). Explains the mechanism, definition, or rationale; teaches rather than instructs.
- Referral (A7): 765 replied questions (14.9%). Points elsewhere: a link, video, store, document, professional, or inspector that plausibly resolves the question.
- Experience report (A3): 701 replied questions (13.6%). Practice-based testimony from personal, regional, or trade experience, with no authority cited.
- Correction (A5): 584 replied questions (11.3%). Corrects the asker's premise, practice, or safety error; may co-occur with a prescription or explanation.
- Social or non-substantive (A10): 531 replied questions (10.3%). Humor, banter, agreement, empathy, argument, insults, promotion, or spam. Always assigned alone.
- Code or authority citation (A4): 400 replied questions (7.8%). Invokes the National Electrical Code, local code, a listing, or a manufacturer requirement.
- Creator meta-response (A8): 342 replied questions (6.6%). The creator addresses the video rather than the question: scope statements, future content promises, acknowledgments.
- Hedged speculation (A9): 194 replied questions (3.8%). Attempts an answer while flagging uncertainty.
- Counter-question (A6): 178 replied questions (3.5%). Requests missing details or clarification instead of answering.

# How solutions are provided in the comment threads

## Top answer families overall

- Raceway Cable Routing (Prescription, 217 answers): These patterns address cable selection, conduit, raceways, pulling, fishing, routing, segregation, and cable management.
- Circuit Sizing and Capacity (Prescription, 212 answers): These patterns concern conductor sizing, ampacity, voltage drop, dedicated circuits, and branch-circuit capacity.
- Grounding Bonding and Electrodes (Prescription, 184 answers): These patterns address grounding conductors, bonding connections, electrodes, grounding continuity, and equipotential safety.
- Equipment Ratings and Compatibility (Prescription, 166 answers): These patterns address equipment ratings, approved assemblies, brand compatibility, substitutions, and purchase due diligence.
- Splicing and Termination Methods (Prescription, 131 answers): These patterns concern conductor preparation, splicing, pigtails, terminal connections, identification, and termination materials.
- Electrical Tools and Work Methods (Prescription, 99 answers): These patterns identify tools, materials, drafting aids, component preparation methods, and practical installation techniques.
- Basic Electrical Relationships (Explanation, 96 answers): These patterns explain fundamental electrical quantities, circuit behavior, and instantaneous waveform values.
- Cable Support and Environmental Protection (Prescription, 88 answers): These patterns specify physical support, mechanical protection, weatherproofing, sealing, and environmental resistance.
- Battery Inverter and Generator Systems (Prescription, 86 answers): These patterns concern batteries, charging, inverters, generators, backup power, and alternate power supplies.
- Grounding and Bonding Paths (Explanation, 84 answers): These patterns explain grounding conductors, bonding connections, fault-current paths, and isolated grounding arrangements.

# How solutions are provided in the comment threads

## One example of each major mechanism

Prescription (A1):
Q: "Why didn't you just leave the existing receptacle and add the new one? Would have been less work." (V:Jpu-3zB8Pqs) (Q:Ugx1hbpmGvfSDaPnqYR4AaABAg)
A: The NEC regulates branch-circuit load rather than a fixed receptacle count. For bathrooms, provide the required 20 A branch circuit and GFCI protection while verifying conductor ampacity, box fill, and grounding/bonding.

Explanation (A2):
Q: "Why didn't you just leave the existing receptacle and add the new one? Would have been less work." (V:Jpu-3zB8Pqs) (Q:Ugx1hbpmGvfSDaPnqYR4AaABAg)
A: The NEC regulates branch-circuit load rather than a fixed receptacle count. For bathrooms, provide the required 20 A branch circuit and GFCI protection while verifying conductor ampacity, box fill, and grounding/bonding.

Code or authority citation (A4):
Q: "Why didn't you just leave the existing receptacle and add the new one? Would have been less work." (V:Jpu-3zB8Pqs) (Q:Ugx1hbpmGvfSDaPnqYR4AaABAg)
A: The NEC regulates branch-circuit load rather than a fixed receptacle count. For bathrooms, provide the required 20 A branch circuit and GFCI protection while verifying conductor ampacity, box fill, and grounding/bonding.

Experience report (A3):
Q: "Stackers missing for 4 cables running down the 2x4 🧐" (V:PrJlFlL9I84) (Q:Ugy9VeakbI-YwEBLXBR4AaABAg)
A: The practical solution offered is to staple the cables to the stud center rather than use stackers, keeping required edge clearance; local inspector interpretation may require nail plates or backing on exterior walls.

Referral (A7):
Q: "What number , group wire you used for 100 amp panel" (V:vAD3r_nF6L4) (Q:UgwGYwKSxMyrTOZmSxF4AaABAg)
A: The primary responder cites NEC Table 250.66 and Table 310.16, implying #6 AWG copper for the grounding conductor and referencing ampacity/terminal temperature requirements for the 100 A installation; verify with the AHJ.

overview.title: ElectriAI knowledge base overview
overview.chunkText:
# ElectriAI knowledge base overview

This knowledge base is built from 16,862 YouTube comment threads on electrical construction videos, analyzed by GPT-5-mini and then classified into a question taxonomy by GPT-5.6 Luna. It covers 14,980 extracted practitioner questions across 398 videos, posted between 2011 and 2025. Each question carries one to three question types, and replied rows carry answer types, drawn from ten substantive question types (a residual class, Q11 social or rhetorical, is excluded from the gap analysis) and ten answer mechanisms (A1 to A10), plus a small untyped bucket for replied rows with no classified mechanism. A consolidation pass grouped the questions into 263 question families and the answers into 204 answer families. All labels are from a single-model v0 pilot and are provisional.

## What you can ask this knowledge base
- Knowledge gaps: which topics practitioners ask about that never get answered (see the knowledge gaps page)
- Trends: how question volume and mix have shifted over the years (see the trends over time page)
- Answering behavior: how solutions get delivered when they come (see the how solutions are provided page)
- Technical content: real practitioner questions and the answers they received, organized into question families covering permissibility, sizing, procedure, theory, troubleshooting, comparisons, sourcing, and more

## The question taxonomy
- Permissibility and compliance (Q1): 1,890 questions. Asks whether a practice, material, or installation is permitted, legal, or code compliant, either in general or in a specific jurisdiction. Template: "Can I [action] [component] in [location or condition]?" or "Is [practice] allowed [in jurisdiction]?"
- Specification and sizing (Q2): 881 questions. Asks for the size, rating, or quantity of a component for a given load or application. Template: "What [size, rating, or quantity] [component] for [load or application] at [distance or condition]?"
- Procedural (Q3): 1,239 questions. Asks how to perform a task, often under a constraint. Template: "How do you [task] when [constraint]?"
- Conceptual (Q4): 2,138 questions. Seeks understanding of why or how an electrical phenomenon behaves the way it does, including asking the video creator to clarify a claim, figure, or moment in the video. Template: "Why or how does [phenomenon] behave this way under [condition]?"
- Diagnostic (Q5): 404 questions. Troubleshooting questions: why a system shows a symptom, or how to fix a problem. Template: "Why does [system] show [symptom] when [trigger]?" or "How do I fix [problem]?"
- Practice justification and challenge (Q6): 1,615 questions. Interrogates a choice the video creator made, usually implying a correction. Template: "Why did you [observed practice] instead of [alternative]?" or "Shouldn't you have [expected practice]?"
- Comparison and alternatives (Q7): 792 questions. Asks to compare options or for alternatives for a use case. Template: "[Option A] or [Option B] for [use case]?" or "What about [alternative] for [context]?"
- Validation and review (Q8): 466 questions. The asker submits their own plan, work, or situation for assessment. Template: "Is [my plan, work, or situation] OK, safe, or compliant? Do you see any problem?"
- Resource identification and sourcing (Q9): 2,270 questions. Asks what an item is called, where to get it, or what it costs. Template: "What is [item] called?", "Where do I get [item]?", or "How much does [item] cost?"
- Content request (Q10): 1,238 questions. Asks the creator to produce content or share an artifact. Template: "Can you make a video about [subject]?" or "Can you share [artifact]?"
- Other, social, or rhetorical (Q11): 2,047 questions. Escape category for questions with no technical substance: jokes, insults, small talk, and rhetorical jabs. Always assigned alone and excluded from the family consolidation and knowledge gap analysis.

## The answer taxonomy
- Prescription (A1). A specific actionable answer, unconditional or conditional: do X, or yes if condition.
- Explanation (A2). Explains the mechanism, definition, or rationale; teaches rather than instructs.
- Experience report (A3). Practice-based testimony from personal, regional, or trade experience, with no authority cited.
- Code or authority citation (A4). Invokes the National Electrical Code, local code, a listing, or a manufacturer requirement.
- Correction (A5). Corrects the asker's premise, practice, or safety error; may co-occur with a prescription or explanation.
- Counter-question (A6). Requests missing details or clarification instead of answering.
- Referral (A7). Points elsewhere: a link, video, store, document, professional, or inspector that plausibly resolves the question.
- Creator meta-response (A8). The creator addresses the video rather than the question: scope statements, future content promises, acknowledgments.
- Hedged speculation (A9). Attempts an answer while flagging uncertainty.
- Social or non-substantive (A10). Humor, banter, agreement, empathy, argument, insults, promotion, or spam. Always assigned alone.

## Corpus outcomes
- Substantive questions (excluding the social or rhetorical escape type): 12,933
- Never received a reply: 7,784 (60.2%)
- Replied but unresolved: 1,482
- Answered: 3,667 (71.2% of the 5,149 replied questions)
